newsitem.title: USA: Lawyer says DNC aide Huang will accept subpoena.
newsitem.headline: Lawyer says DNC aide Huang will accept subpoena.

text.p: Lawyers for Democratic National Committee (DNC) official John Huang said Friday he will accept a subpoena in a civil lawsuit by a conservative legal group against the Commerce Department.

"Our client will be in the District of Columbia on Monday morning. We will arrange to have service of the deposition subpoena completed at or before that time," lawyers John Kenney and Ty Cobb said in a letter.
They sent the letter to Democratic Party chairman Don Fowler, who had followed a judge's orders and instructed Huang to report to work on Monday so the subpoena could be served.

Huang left the Commerce Department in December to become vice-chairman of the Democratic National Committee's finance arm. He was removed from his fund-raising duties last week after questions were raised about contributions he helped solicit, but he remains a DNC employee.
Federal marshals have been looking for Huang since Wednesday to give him the subpoena so he can be questioned next Tuesday. They have been unable to find him.
An attorney for Huang told the judge he would not be available for questioning until Nov. 6, a day after the elections, at the earliest.

The case involved a two-year-old lawsuit by the group Judicial Watch claiming the Commerce Department failed to release documents requested under the freedom-of-information law on trade missions led by late Commerce Secretary Ron Brown.
Huang initially was not mentioned in the lawsuit, but the group sought him for questioning after he was cited in news reports about his fund-raising activities.

The chairman of the House Oversight Committee, the House Judiciary Committee, and the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee sent a letter to President Clinton calling on him to respond immediately to questions about DNC fund-raising.
The letter also expressed grave concern about Huang's disappearance and said Huang "appears to be evading federal marshals who are searching for him to enforce a subpoena."
